comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implemented on branch fix/9ec0-reconciler-drain (commit 7af470bc4), committed locally, NOT pushed.

## Verified against the tree (gerrit/main 36e986c188)

Root cause confirmed by reading: `app.py` lifespan awaits `queue.join()` only; `reconcile_once`
awaits `review_and_vote` INLINE with `gerrit=`/`dedup=` injected, outside that queue. With an
empty queue the join returns at once and the reconcile task is cancelled within
`shutdown_cancel_seconds()` (10s).

CORRECTION to this ticket's "Suspected fix": it proposes waiting on `voter.in_flight_reviews()`
"that 34cd added". That symbol does NOT exist on gerrit/main — 34cd's work is on an unpushed
local branch (db241b80ab), and `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` has no defer logic either. So the
deploy-side mitigation is not in the tree, and this fix had to be self-contained.

## Shape chosen: cooperative stop + a gated, budget-shared wait

Rejected "route reconciler reviews through the worker queue": the queue is fire-and-forget, so
`reconcile_once`'s `{scanned, reviewed}` return (asserted in 6 tests) becomes unobtainable; the
worker does NOT inject gerrit/dedup so the shared-client reuse is lost; and with WORKER_COUNT=1
backfill would serialize behind webhook work, which today runs concurrently as a separate task.

Implemented instead: `reconcile.request_stop()` makes the loop take no NEW candidate and return
once the in-flight review lands, so the reconcile task itself is awaitable as a drain. The
lifespan requests the stop BEFORE either wait, drains the queue, then waits for the reconcile
task — gated on `review_in_flight()`.

## Bounding

Both halves share ONE `shutdown_drain_seconds()` deadline. Independent windows would allow 2x1200s;
with the 60s store-lock budget the floor would be 2460s against a 1320s stop_grace_period, so
sharing the deadline is what keeps the existing grace-period relationship true (floor stays 1260s).
`asyncio.wait`, not `wait_for` — wait_for's timeout path cancels then awaits unboundedly, which
re-broke the c2ba hang and was caught by the existing c2ba test.

The `review_in_flight()` gate exists because an unconditional wait made a reconciler parked in a
blocking events-log fetch hold the FULL budget (a real regression: ~10s shutdown becomes minutes).

## Tests

RED proven before the fix, and each guard mutation-tested as load-bearing. Coverage is placed in
the DEFAULT tier as well as the lifespan, because CI's pytest lane installs only `[dev]` and every
`pytest.importorskip("fastapi")` test SKIPS there — 9 skips in this file, including the existing
shutdown-drain and c2ba bounded-shutdown tests. Lifespan-only coverage would have been a skip in CI.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Overlap with 34cd worth resolving when both land

34cd's unpushed branch adds `voter.in_flight_reviews()` — a counter bracketed around
`review_and_vote`, counting BOTH the worker and the reconciler, exposed on `/health` for
autodeploy to poll. This change adds `reconcile.review_in_flight()`, counting the RECONCILER
only, used in-process by the lifespan.

They are independent by design (this fix cannot depend on unlanded work), but whichever lands
second should consolidate: a single counter in `voter` could serve both the `/health` field and
this drain gate. Note the two are not interchangeable as-is — the lifespan gate specifically
needs "is the RECONCILER mid-review", because a WORKER review in flight is already covered by
`queue.join()`, and gating on a combined count would make the reconciler wait redundant-but-
harmless rather than wrong. Flagged so the merge is deliberate rather than accidental.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## CORRECTION: 34cd LANDED mid-session; rebased and consolidated

My earlier comment said 34cd was unpushed. That was true of my base (36e986c188) but went stale
during the session: 34cd landed on gerrit/main as e9d4d390c3 ("34cd: defer autodeploy while a
review runs"). So `voter.in_flight_reviews()` and the autodeploy defer DO now exist on main.

Rebased onto gerrit/main (1920dc9fe5) — textually clean, because 34cd touched only the `/health`
route in app.py, not the lifespan. Then DROPPED my own reconciler-scoped counter and gated the
drain on `voter.in_flight_reviews()` instead, rather than shipping two counters for one fact.

The gate cannot go stale in either direction: the stop is requested before either wait so no new
reconciler review can start, and `queue.join()` has already returned so any remaining count is
the reconciler's. Had the join timed out instead, a worker review could still be counted — but
then the shared budget is spent, so the wait is a no-op.

## Test-fidelity trap this surfaced, worth recording

Consolidating onto voter's counter broke my lifespan tests, because they stubbed
`review_and_vote` — and `_counting_in_flight` lives INSIDE it, so the count stayed 0 and the gate
never fired. The tempting fix (have the stub hold the count itself) would have made the test
assert against a number it manufactured — the exact "guard shares the bug's assumption" shape.

Instead the lifespan tests now slow the GATE (`produce_code_review_verdict`) so the REAL
`review_and_vote` runs and genuinely holds the count, and completion is read from a vote actually
being cast rather than from a stub's transcript. Relevant because 34cd's
`test_the_reconciler_path_is_counted_too` is a SOURCE-TEXT assertion (it greps reconcile.py for
`review_and_vote`), not a behavioural one, so it was too thin to lean on for this gate.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Stranded work RECLAIMED and pushed — Gerrit change 1617

Adopted the unpushed commit ecb71a79f8 from worktree ~/fix-9ec0 (operator-approved above) and
rebased it onto current origin/main. The DESIGN survived review unchanged — cooperative
`request_stop()` + a single shared `shutdown_drain_seconds()` deadline, gated on
`voter.in_flight_reviews()`. Three adaptations were needed, and two of them were real defects
rather than textual conflicts.

### 1. The stop path violated the cursor low-water-mark invariant (bug 9f63)

The only TEXTUAL conflict was additive (both sides inserted at the same point in reconcile.py).
The SEMANTIC conflict was silent: 9f63 landed while this branch sat idle and made the reconcile
cursor a LOW-WATER MARK. 9ec0's shutdown `break` skipped remaining candidates WITHOUT recording
them in `held_back`, so `_persist_cursor` still advanced the cursor to `newest` and pushed those
candidates outside the next pass's inclusive `?t1=` window — unreachable forever.

That made shutdown the one path that silently drops a gap patchset, which is precisely the defect
9f63 closed. The original commit's comment ("the next container's startup pass picks it straight
back up") was therefore false on the new base. Fixed by recording every remaining candidate in
`held_back`. Proven RED against the un-held-back version, using the 9f63 oracle shape: the skipped
candidate is NOT the newest event, so unrelated chatter drags `newest` past it — the only shape in
which the defect can be expressed.

### 2. Six tests were silently neutered by a new autouse fixture

Main grew `_safe_review_bot_lifespan_defaults`, which swaps `reconcile_loop` for an idle stub
unless a test carries `@pytest.mark.real_reconcile_loop`. The six tests here that drive the REAL
loop predate it, so they HUNG rather than failed — an infinite `while not started: await sleep()`
with no cap. Markers added. Worth noting the failure mode: a busy-wait probe turns a neutered
dependency into a hang, not a red test.

### 3. ASYNC110

Ruff now flags the probes' `while ...: await asyncio.sleep(...)` polls. The rule's suggested
`asyncio.Event` is NOT usable here — the probes are appended from worker threads (the review gate
and the events-log fetch both run off-loop via `to_thread`) and an asyncio.Event may not be set
from another thread. Waiting on a `threading.Event` would consume an executor thread the code
under test needs. Resolved with one `_await_probe` helper that polls inside a single `to_thread`
hop, which keeps the event loop free — the property the rule actually protects.

### Gates

`make lint` = 0, `make typecheck` = 0, `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` 90 passed / 13 skipped
(fastapi absent locally, as in CI's `[dev]` lane — which is why the stop semantics are also
covered in the default tier). Broader selection: 2582 passed. The 2 errors in
`test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py` (`No module named 'alert_dedup'`) reproduce on a clean
origin/main and are unrelated to this change.

Plan-review re-earned in this environment (the prior attestation was `foreign_key`): PASS, 0
blocking.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## CI triage on patch set 1: two REAL failures, neither an infra flake

`Verified -1` on change 1617 PS1 was not the known shallow-clone flake — it was two genuine
failures, both caused by main moving during the 40h strand. Reproduced locally after installing
the `reviewbot` extra (my earlier local run lacked fastapi, so the whole lifespan tier SKIPPED —
that gap is why the first push looked green).

### A. A real defect in the adopted design: the stop flag outlived its shutdown

`test_accepted_rerun_survives_restart_via_gerrit_reconcile` failed DETERMINISTICALLY on all four
lanes with `{'scanned': 1, 'reviewed': 0}`. Root cause: `_stop_requested` is module state on
`reconcile`, not per-app, and was cleared only at lifespan STARTUP. That test exits the lifespan
and then re-drives the rerun the discarded in-memory queue lost — the replacement-process
recovery path — so it ran `reconcile_once` with the flag still SET and the pass declined
everything.

This is a production defect, not a test artifact: after any lifespan shutdown, every later
`reconcile_once` in that process silently reviews nothing while still reporting the candidates as
`scanned`, so it reads as "nothing was owed a vote" rather than as a fault. That is precisely the
silent-backfill-failure mode 9ec0 exists to prevent. The flag now clears at the END of shutdown,
after the bounded cancel, so it cannot outlive the shutdown that set it. Added a test pinning the
post-shutdown state directly rather than only via that oracle's side effects.

Worth recording: the original commit's rationale said CI's pytest lane installs only `[dev]` so
the fastapi tier skips there. That is FALSE for this lane — CI ran 11945 tests including the
lifespan tier. The default-tier duplication was still worth having, but the stated reason for it
was wrong.

### B. A new wall-clock-assert lint, right about 3 of its 4 findings

Main grew `scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py` while this branch sat (upper-bound wall-clock
asserts are a proven flake class). Rather than blanket-sanctioning:

- The AC2 test's `elapsed < 3.0` was REDUNDANT and is gone: a drain that re-extended would have
  to start a second review, which its `len(started) == 1` already catches structurally.
- The shared-deadline and in-flight-gate tests now read the timeout the drain was actually
  HANDED, via a spy on the lifespan's `asyncio.wait`, instead of timing it. Strictly stronger — a
  stopwatch also passes if the wait runs and happens to return fast — and it fails in the SAFE
  direction, since a loaded runner leaves LESS budget remaining, never more. Both were
  mutation-checked (removed gate; independent window) and both go red.
- Only the idle-stop test keeps a ceiling, sanctioned as a hang-guard: its failure mode is
  waiting out a 3600s interval, so a 5s ceiling dwarfs the ~0.25s actually needed.

Gates on the new base: lint 0, typecheck 0, wall-clock 0, `test_review_bot.py` 104 passed / 0
skipped. Patch set 2 pushed.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The review-bot's shutdown drain covers only HALF of its review paths.

`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`'s lifespan does:

    await asyncio.wait_for(queue.join(), timeout=shutdown_drain_seconds())

then cancels every task, bounded by `shutdown_cancel_seconds()` (10s).

`queue.join()` waits for the webhook QUEUE to empty, so a webhook-queued review IS protected
(1200s drain, and compose grants `stop_grace_period: 1320s` — both far exceed the ~10 min review).

But `reconcile.reconcile_once` awaits `review_and_vote` INLINE, not through the queue. When the
queue is empty, `queue.join()` returns IMMEDIATELY and the `reconcile_loop` task is cancelled
within ~10s — abandoning a backfill review that may be minutes in.

Found while implementing [rebar:34cd-1a7c-b9b1-4b05]; verified by reading origin/main d4095763e3.

## Why it matters independently of 34cd

34cd fixes this from the DEPLOY side: autodeploy now defers a container recreation while
`/health` reports `in_flight > 0`, so the autodeploy path no longer kills reconciler reviews.

The underlying drain gap is untouched by that. ANY other container stop still kills a reconciler
review with effectively no drain:
  - an operator `docker compose restart` / `up -d` run by hand
  - `compose-up.sh` during a manual deploy
  - a host reboot / systemd stop
  - the rollback path inside autodeploy itself (`docker compose up -d` after re-tagging `:prev`)

The reconciler is also the path that RETRIES a review killed by anything else, so the gap sits on
the self-heal path. And it is silent for the same reason 34cd was: a cancelled review fails
nothing, so no `VOTER_ERROR` is emitted and `restarts` stays 0.

## Suspected fix

Make the drain cover in-flight reconciler work, not just the queue — e.g. have the lifespan wait
on the same in-flight review count that 34cd added (`voter.in_flight_reviews()`) under the
existing `shutdown_drain_seconds()` budget, before cancelling tasks. The budget and
`stop_grace_period` are already sized for a full review, so this likely needs no new tunables.

Note the ordering constraint: the wait must not let a reconcile pass START a NEW review while
draining, or shutdown could be extended repeatedly. The reconciler probably needs a
stop-accepting-new-work signal alongside the drain.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reconciler review in flight at shutdown is drained (bounded by the existing
      `shutdown_drain_seconds()`), not cancelled within `shutdown_cancel_seconds()`.
- [ ] The drain does not extend indefinitely: no new review may start once shutdown has begun,
      proven by a test.
- [ ] The existing webhook-queue drain behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
compiled_state.title: Shutdown drain misses the reconciler's in-flight review, so any container stop kills it
